newsitem.title: NORWAY: Car bomb explodes outside Oslo biker club.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb explodes outside Oslo biker club.

text.p: A powerful car bomb exploded outside the headquarters of a Norwegian motorcycle gang on Wednesday, causing extensive damage but no injuries, in the latest round of a violent Nordic biker war.

Police said the bomb exploded shortly after midnight (2300 GMT) beneath a stolen car parked outside the Oslo headquarters of MC Norway, grouping bikers aspiring to join the international Hell's Angels.
The blast burned out the car, shattered windows and damaged a wooden gate.

"No doubt the bomb was powerful," a police spokesman said. "A building 40 metres (yards) from the site of the explosion was also damaged. We heard the bang at the police station about three kilometres (two miles) away."

Police said they were looking for two men believed to be members of the rival Bandidos motorcycle gang. MC Norway members in the building told police they recognised the men, who were filmed by a security camera.
Conflict between the gangs, both local offshoots of U.S. groups with extensive European networks, began almost as soon as the Bandidos set up shop in the region in the summer of 1993.

The latest incident came after Norway beefed up surveillance of local biker groups following a missile attack three weeks ago on a Hell's Angels clubhouse in central Copenhagen that killed two people.
That was the bloodiest single incident so far in a turf war that has killed five people and wounded many others this year in Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden.
Nordic governments, worried that motorcycle gangs are seeking to turn a traditionally peaceful region into a battlefield, have begun squeezing the bikers out of their cities.
But no efforts have been made so far to evict MC Norway from the Oslo industrial area where a woman was shot and wounded in the head when her car drove slowly past its headquarters last May.
In January shots were fired from the same building at a car belonging to the rival motorcycle gang Outlaws. One Outlaw member was hit in the arm.
In other incidents in Norway, a bullet was fired at a car driven by a Hells Angel's member in central Oslo in July, days after a Danish member of the Bandidos was shot dead in Drammen, south of Oslo.
